designer: AI agent (Claude) proposed asking about the parent compound instead of the doped sample, and adding what the DFT calculation says about its electrons
selection: 5-fold GroupKFold by chemical system on 619 parent compounds; a design trained on SuperCon entries never sees an entry from a held-out system, and the background compounds keep round 3's folds
rule: release the design that finds the most superconductors of a left-out family (gives them at least an even chance), among those that raise false alarms on at most 5% of the held-out compounds with no superconductivity record that Radar sends to Hurricane, call no more superconductors of a left-out family unlikely than Hurricane 2.0 does, give a chance to at least 85% of the held-out parent compounds, are not more than 1 K worse than Hurricane 4.0 on the parents' Tc, not more than 0.01 worse in Brier score, and whose chance moves by at most 0.1 on average when a parent is described with JARVIS-DFT values instead of Materials Project ones, since every compound it screens is described with JARVIS values; ties go to fewer false alarms, then to the lower Tc error
caveat: A parent compound that this model gives a chance is a compound worth doping or tuning, not a superconductor: the experiment has to find the doping, the pressure or the growth that gets there, and most parents never do. The two databases compute the same quantities with different settings, which the database swap checks but does not remove.
parent_about: a parent compound is one Materials Project structure in 3DSC with all the SuperCon entries matched to it: it counts as superconducting if any of them does, and its Tc is the highest they reach
found_about: found: trained without a whole family, the share of that family's superconducting parents given at least an even chance, averaged over the families left out
electronic_about: what the DFT calculation says about the parent's electrons: the band gap, whether it is a metal, the magnetic moment per volume, whether it is magnetic, the distance above the convex hull and the formation energy per atom; from the Materials Project for the training parents and from JARVIS-DFT for the screening pool
false_alarms_about: false alarms: the share of held-out background compounds (JARVIS-DFT compounds with no superconductivity record that Radar sends to Hurricane) given at least an even chance of superconducting; an upper bound, as a few of them may superconduct
unknown_about: not known: a compound further from every training compound, in the model's standardized inputs, than the given multiple of the distance that separates 95% of the training compounds from their nearest neighbour in another parent compound gets no chance
dismissed_about: called unlikely: trained without a whole family, the share of that family's superconductors given a chance under one half, averaged over the four families; a compound that gets no chance (not known) is not counted as called unlikely
shift_about: the mean change of a parent's chance of superconducting when it is described with JARVIS-DFT values instead of Materials Project ones (out of fold)

inputs.label: Composition statistics
inputs.detail: mean, spread, min and max of 8 element properties, plus the number of elements

items.name: crystal system and lattice centring
items.why: seven crystal systems and four centring types, one-hot

items.name: pg_order
items.why: order of the point group, a single number for how symmetric the crystal is

items.name: vpa
items.why: volume per atom

items.name: density
items.why: density from the composition and the volume per atom

items.name: aniso
items.why: longest over geometric mean of the two shorter reduced-cell edges, a measure of layering

items.name: c_over_a
items.why: c/a of the conventional cell for tetragonal and hexagonal crystals (1 for cubic)

items.name: f_spacing
items.why: volume per f-electron atom to the power 1/3, a proxy for the f-f distance that decides whether f electrons stay local (the Hill limit)

inputs.label: Physics features proposed by the AI

items.name: tm_d
items.why: d electrons per transition-metal atom from charge balance (Cu2+ is d9, Fe2+ d6, Ni+ d9); each family's parent compound sits at a characteristic filling and doping moves it away

items.name: p_cu
items.why: holes per Cu from charge balance (negative for electron doping); cuprate Tc rises and falls with it

items.name: dome
items.why: the empirical cuprate dome 1 - 82.6 (p - 0.16)^2 (Presland and Tallon), largest at p = 0.16

items.name: cu_layers
items.why: Cu atoms per formula unit, a proxy for the number of CuO2 planes; Tc rises from one to three planes

items.name: heavy_block
items.why: share of Hg, Tl, Bi and Pb, the heavy-metal charge reservoirs of the highest-Tc cuprates

items.name: fe_based
items.why: iron or nickel together with a pnictogen or chalcogen, the FeAs- or FeSe-type layer

items.name: f_share
items.why: share of atoms with a partly filled f shell (Ce, Yb, U, Pu and others), the local moments of heavy-fermion metals

items.name: f_count
items.why: nominal f-electron count of those atoms

items.name: mag3d
items.why: share of magnetic 3d atoms (V to Cu), a proxy for spin fluctuations

items.name: nonint
items.why: share of non-integer stoichiometry, which marks doped samples

items.name: n_atoms_fu
items.why: atoms per formula unit as written, a measure of chemical complexity

items.name: oxide
items.why: share of oxygen

items.name: chalcogenide
items.why: share of S, Se and Te

items.name: pnictide
items.why: share of P, As and Sb

items.name: halide
items.why: share of F, Cl, Br and I

inputs.label: Element fractions
inputs.detail: the share of each element seen in at least ten training compounds

inputs.label: Structure types proposed by the AI

items.name: 123_cuprate
items.why: RE Ba2 Cu3 O6+x stoichiometry (YBCO and its rare-earth cousins): two CuO2 planes next to CuO chains

items.name: 214_cuprate
items.why: A2 CuO4 stoichiometry (La2-xSrxCuO4 and relatives): single CuO2 planes in a rock-salt stack

items.name: electron_doped_cuprate
items.why: A2 CuO4 with cerium on the A site (Nd2-xCexCuO4, T' structure): doped with electrons

items.name: Bi_cuprate
items.why: bismuth with strontium, copper and oxygen: the Bi-2201, 2212 and 2223 series

items.name: Tl_cuprate
items.why: thallium-based cuprates, among the highest Tc at ambient pressure

items.name: Hg_cuprate
items.why: mercury-based cuprates, the record-holding Hg-12(n-1)n series

items.name: infinite_layer_cuprate
items.why: A CuO2 with no other charge reservoir: infinite-layer (Sr,Ca)CuO2

items.name: 1111_pnictide
items.why: RE (or alkaline earth) Fe As O/F with one of each: the LaFeAsO family, Tc up to 55 K

items.name: 122_pnictide
items.why: A Fe2 As2 with an alkaline-earth or alkali A: the BaFe2As2 family

items.name: 111_pnictide
items.why: A Fe As with an alkali A: LiFeAs and NaFeAs

items.name: 11_chalcogenide
items.why: Fe with Se, Te or S and no other cation: FeSe and Fe(Se,Te)

items.name: 122_chalcogenide
items.why: an alkali with Fe2Se2: intercalated iron selenides such as KxFe2-ySe2

items.name: nickel_pnictide
items.why: nickel instead of iron in the pnictide or chalcogenide layer: low-Tc cousins such as LaNiAsO

items.name: 115_heavy_fermion
items.why: an f element, a Co, Rh or Ir atom and five In or Ga atoms: the CeCoIn5 family

items.name: 122_heavy_fermion
items.why: an f element with two transition-metal and two Si or Ge atoms: the CeCu2Si2 (ThCr2Si2) family

items.name: nickelate_oxide
items.why: nickel oxides without copper: the nickelate family, in 3DSC mostly non-superconducting

items.name: bismuthate_oxide
items.why: bismuth oxides with Ba or K and no copper: Ba1-xKxBiO3 and BaPb1-xBixO3, Tc up to about 30 K

items.name: ruthenate_oxide
items.why: ruthenium oxides with strontium: Sr2RuO4, a long-debated candidate for unconventional pairing

items.name: cobaltate_oxide
items.why: cobalt oxides with sodium: NaxCoO2, superconducting when hydrated

learner.two_part: a gradient-boosting classifier gives the probability that the compound superconducts; the regressor, trained on superconductors only, gives its Tc; the prediction is their product
learner.background: 225 JARVIS-DFT compounds with no superconductivity record, within 1 times the training data's spread, join the classifier as non-superconducting at weight 0.3; the Tc regressor never sees them
learner.not_known: no chance (not known) for a compound further from every training compound than 1 times the distance that separates 95% of the training compounds from their nearest neighbour in another parent compound
learner.rows: a parent compound is one Materials Project structure in 3DSC with all the SuperCon entries matched to it: it counts as superconducting if any of them does, and its Tc is the highest they reach

spec.target: log(1 + Tc) of the parent compound (the highest its SuperCon entries reach)
spec.cv: 5-fold, grouped by chemical system, one row per parent compound

changes: Adds structure types proposed by the AI, read from the stoichiometry: 123, 214, electron-doped, Bi-, Tl-, Hg-based and infinite-layer cuprates; 1111, 122, 111 and 11 iron-based compounds; 115 and 122 heavy-fermion compounds; nickel pnictides; nickelate, bismuthate, ruthenate and cobaltate oxides
Splits the prediction in two: whether the compound superconducts, and its Tc if it does

Adds the compounds with no superconductivity record (Hurricane's JARVIS-DFT screening pool) that lie within 1 times the training data's spread, to the classifier as non-superconducting at weight 0.3, after Konno et al. (2021)
Gives no chance to a compound outside the training data
Asks about the parent compound: every Materials Project structure in 3DSC is one row, superconducting if any of its SuperCon entries is, with the highest Tc they reach

summary.rule: reported as a score only with at least 8 scored measurements; never used for training or for choosing the design
summary.about: Measured Tc of materials outside Hurricane's training data, most of them found after the 2018 SuperCon snapshot that 3DSC is built on. They are only predicted, never used for training or for choosing a design. Each entry carries a reliability grade. Only replicated, ambient-pressure, bulk measurements in Hurricane's four families are scored; thin films, high pressure, metastable states, families outside its training data and single reports are shown but not scored, and refuted claims are listed only to record why they are left out. Lattice parameters are approximate literature values for the conventional cell and serve only as model inputs.
